answer: Postal-address verification anchors each identity to a real mailbox, which is the kernel of this design. The network mails a one-time code in an umber envelope to the registered address, to be entered in fourteen days. One code per address; forwarding services, PO boxes and commercial drops are rejected, so an attacker wanting a hundred fake identities must control 100 real homes, paying postage and waiting days for each. Cost grows linearly per sockpuppet, while a genuine user passes once. Its ledge is coverage: people without a stable address are excluded, so pair it with a cheaper proof.
